text:
ashley: quick brain dump after today's offload sync. i sketched a flow where we treat tenant arenas as "logical" only (no dedicated phys slabs) and use a tag-based compactor to reduce fragmentation. want feedback on atomicity model.
ran: sounds promising. main question: how do we ensure a running kernel doesn't deref a pointer while we relocate? blocking the kernel is expensive.
oscar: we avoid kernel stops by shifting indirection: all allocations return a token -> internal descriptor table. kernels read pointer via descriptor. compaction updates descriptor atomically. cost: one extra indirection per access.
mina: that adds latency per token deref though. what about making it conditional: hot paths use direct ptr, cold objects go via descriptor. then compactor only touches descriptor-backed objects.
ashley: conditional indirection increases complexity (two lookup paths). we'd need a flag per allocation marking 'movable'. maybe default small objects movable, large pinned by default.
ran: good idea. add a "pinned_hint" flag to allocate API so low-latency embeddings can opt out. API example: `allocate(tenant, size, flags) -> alloc_id`. flags: MOVABLE|PINNED|LOW_LATENCY.
oscar: how to do the actual move? proposal: 1) allocate target slab, 2) memcpy objects -> target, 3) publish new descriptors with atomic CAS, 4) wait for prior readers via epoch/rcu grace period, 5) free old slab.
mina: step 4 is tricky. RCU grace period requires kernel cooperation or epoch tracking per inference. we already have request tokens; can we tie epoch to request lifecycle? each inference increments in-flight counter for slabs it touches.
ashley: tie-in with kv-cache pin API: when a request pins a kv entry, it increments slab refcount. compactor marks slab draining and waits for refcount==0 or timeout. add backoff + skip if can't drain.
ran: timeout behavior needs defaults. i'd prefer exponential backoff then mark slab 'sticky' to avoid thrashing. also emit metric `compactor.skipped_drains`.
oscar: cross-node moves? moving across hosts for Dedicated clusters may require network copy. prefer local consolidation first; only export ownership if eviction pressure persists for N minutes.
mina: security note: for Private deployments, tenants==orgs. controller policy must allow admins to choose STRICT_ISOLATION which bypasses tagging and enforces dedicated arenas. doc that as enterprise opt-in.
ashley: telemetry: compactness = 1 - (used_bytes / allocated_bytes). expose per-tenant histogram and a rolling 24h percentile. plus `migration_latency` and `migration_cpu_seconds`.
ran: instrumentation idea: track pre/post tail latency for a tenant during compaction windows. auto-disable aggressive compaction if p99 worsens by >10%.
oscar: operational safety: compactor must have an operator toggle `max_concurrent_migrations`. default 2. also `migration_window` hours.
mina: canary plan: run compactor in dev-tenant with allow_background_migration=true, max_concurrent_migrations=1. run on off-peak hours and capture trace.
ashley: ACLs and API names. propose: public API remains `allocate/free/pin/unpin/query_compactness/mark_draining`. controller exposes `tenant_policy` mapping SLA->strategy (shared, soft-reserve, isolated). do not expose percent-of-host-staging to tenants.
ran: i like that. keep tenant-facing surface small.
oscar: gotcha: pinned CUDA buffers can't be memcpy'd from host. we should prefer migrating host-backed pages first. if pinned device buffers need relocation, fall back to model-level reload or reject aggressive compaction. record `migration_failures.pinned_device`.
mina: also add a scheduler hint for migration cost: `estimated_copy_work` so controller can schedule heavy jobs during low utilization.
ashley: action items: - mina: write canary runbook + failure modes - oscar: prototype descriptor table + atomic swap in allocator shim - ran: add metrics list and dashboard wireframe - ashley: update controller policy draft and enterprise isolation docs
compactor-bot: enqueued canary job for dev-tenant (job_id=canary-2024-07-15-01). ETA 3m.
mina: i'll kick it off and attach traces. please keep a close eye on kv-cache miss spikes.
ashley: perfect. we'll regroup after canary with perf numbers and any correctness surprises.
